profiles.contour: contour, whose src/{coro,net} and crispy's generic half become core-cpp; crispy's renderer half stays, so `crispy::` is rewritten symbol by symbol, never as a prefix
profiles.endo: endo, whose src/tui, the generic half of src/platform and the src/testing helpers become core-cpp; endo::platform keeps Process, Pipe and the process providers
profiles.tuidu: tuidu, whose June snapshot of endo's src/{coro,platform,testing,tui} becomes core-cpp; its crispy::cli types are spelled in an older case
profiles.fastcached: fastcached, whose Async/ and Net/ layers and the moved Core/ files become core-cpp, PascalCase members becoming camelBack

rows.note: Require and Guarantee are here; SoftRequire and fatal() moved to <core/log/Assert.hpp>, so a file using those needs that include added
the factories moved into IoBackend.hpp; there is no DefaultBackend.hpp, because each platform's DefaultBackend.cpp defines them and CMake compiles exactly one

EventSource became IoBackend: a backend dispatches readiness to the ReadinessHandler callbacks a caller registers, instead of returning ready tokens for the caller to route. FdToken, WaitOutcome and FdRegistry are gone with it
the concrete backends are private now (posix/PollBackend.hpp, windows/WfmoBackend.hpp): a program gets one from makeDefaultBackend() or makeBackend(BackendKind), which IoBackend.hpp declares
core::testing::ScopedTempDir has no default prefix, and throws where TempDir failed a REQUIRE; path() and operator/ are unchanged
core-cpp's Types.hpp includes no <windows.h>, <io.h> or <fcntl.h> and defines no STDIN_FILENO or SIGINT: a consumer that relied on those includes its own
endo's and tuidu's crispy snapshots still spell the class `flags`
moves header too: fatal() and SoftRequire() are in <core/log/Assert.hpp>, not <core/Assert.hpp>
read() now returns std::expected<ChannelResult, PlatformError>: test isEndOfStream() where the code tested for 0, and empty() where it tested for a would-block

the shape changed with the name: attach() takes a ReadinessHandler whose callbacks the backend invokes, setInterest() is separate and reports the kernel's refusal as std::expected<void, NetError>, and wait() dispatches rather than returning a WaitOutcome
Interest::None still means 'mute the handle without detaching it', and now means it on every backend
the enumerators gained Iocp, Wfmo, HostDriven, Scripted and Null, and a Last sentinel
readiness is scripted against a HandlerId, handed out in attach order, in place of an FdToken; pushFailure() is new and models the hangup a kernel volunteers
renamed so the row for the table it lives in reads as a table and not as a backend

Task B1. fastcached's SECOND SyncRun -- the overload taking a callable that retrieves the park -- is a name of its own here, core::async::syncRunWith(task, retrieve), declared in the same header. The table keys on the source symbol, so it cannot carry a second row: the rewrite turns every SyncRun into syncRun, and a two-argument call then fails to compile, which names the site to change by hand. That is deliberate -- the alternative is a call that compiles and means something else.
Task B1. Its own header here, where fastcached keeps it in Task.hpp.
Task B1. An executor's parked-work entry; only an executor implementation names it.
Task B1. Every class deriving from it says `using IExecutor::submit;`, or its own submit(std::coroutine_handle<>) hides the base's submit(ParkedWork) (LASTRADA-Software/fastcached#1041).
Task B1. Header-only here: fastcached's ThreadPoolExecutor.cpp is inlined, so a consumer links nothing new for it. Not in the WebAssembly subset.

Task B1. It is built over core::async::IExecutor rather than fastcached's IReactor, so the constructor's first argument changes type: an EventLoop still satisfies it. Its members become camelBack -- push, pop, isClosed, size, hasWaiter, displaced, each a row below -- except Close: the table keys a member row on (profile, name) and ISocket::Close already holds it, so AsyncQueue::Close -> close is recorded here rather than rewritten. Its pop() is also stop-aware now: a cancel from the awaiting flow's own token throws core::async::OperationCancelled, where fastcached's could only answer nullopt on close.

Task B1. Its `bool accepted` is `AsyncQueueAdmission admission`: a bool result reporting success is a finding (.agent/rules/design-principles.md). No rewrite row, for the reason core::tui::LanguageId::Endo has none -- the TYPE changes with the name, so every use site needs a human: `if (queue.Push(x).accepted)` becomes `if (queue.push(x).admission == AsyncQueueAdmission::Accepted)`. `displaced` keeps its name and meaning.

Task B1. It also empties the task, which fastcached's does -- but here the awaiter takes the frame too, so a Task awaited with co_await std::move(t) is empty afterwards and t.handle(), t.done() and t.result() no longer answer about it.
Task B1. The table keys a member row on (profile, name), so this one row carries Submit for every executor: ThreadPoolExecutor's override and EventLoop's are the same rename.
a shape change, not a rename: the awaitable aggregate SleepUntil{&reactor, tp} becomes a call on the loop
a shape change: the aggregate takes the loop, the stop token and the deadline as arguments
*Listener::Bind(...) becomes the free function listen(loop, ListenOptions); the arguments regroup

rows.note: core-cpp takes no dependency on GSL; each use becomes a reference where the callee never rebinds, or a pointer with Require()

the unqualified global Overloaded of <crispy/Overloaded.hpp> is core::Overloaded now; too common a word to rewrite unqualified
a namespace DEFINITION is not mechanical: only a human can tell a consumer's own namespace from the moved one. endo has five such forward declarations
stays in endo: it is shell-specific. Its namespace is not rewritten, which is why endo::testing has symbol rows rather than a namespace row

core::tui ships no consumer's language (Task B13a, core-cpp#24). endo registers its own through core::tui::SyntaxHighlighterRegistry::registerLanguage({.name="endo", .extensions={".endo"}, .fenceTags={"endo"}, .highlight=highlightEndoLine}), which returns std::expected<LanguageId, LanguageRegistrationFailure>; *result is the id to use in place of this one, and it belongs to that registry -- hold one registry per program, or keep each id with the registry that issued it. No rewrite row: the call shape changes, so a compile error here is the better signal.

the process-wide registration callback is gone (Task B13a, core-cpp#24). The application owns a core::tui::SyntaxHighlighterRegistry, fills it once at startup and passes it to MarkdownRenderer, StyledText::fromMarkdown, detectLanguageFromPath and highlightLine, each of which takes it as a trailing argument defaulting to nullptr.

a backend has no registration tokens any more: the ReadinessHandler's ADDRESS is its registration's identity, and detach() takes the handler. EventLoop keeps an id of its own for its parks (core::net::ParkId), which is internal to the loop.
a wait dispatches instead of reporting: IoBackend::wait invokes the handler callbacks and answers a WaitResult, which carries only how many of them ran.

the shared registration list, with FdRegistration, is gone: each backend keeps whatever its kernel needs (poll a vector, epoll and kqueue a map keyed by handler, with the private dup() a duplicate registration requires).

split in two and made private: core::net::PollBackend (posix/PollBackend.hpp) and core::net::WfmoBackend (windows/WfmoBackend.hpp). Reach one through makeBackend(BackendKind::Poll) or makeDefaultBackend().
core::net::EpollBackend (linux/EpollBackend.hpp), still private; reach it through makeBackend(BackendKind::Epoll).
core::net::KqueueBackend (bsd/KqueueBackend.hpp), still private; reach it through makeBackend(BackendKind::Kqueue).
